name: How much does commercial construction cost per square foot, and why do estimates vary so much?

mainEntity.name: How much does commercial construction cost per square foot, and why do estimates vary so much?

acceptedAnswer.text:
1. DIRECT ANSWER
Commercial construction can range widely per square foot based on location, building type, and finish level; two projects of the same size can legitimately have very different costs. Early “ballpark” numbers are useful but never final.

2. CONTEXT
Cost is driven by structure, systems, code upgrades, and tenant-specific needs, not just finishes. Owners often compare incompatible estimates (different scopes or assumptions) and think someone is overcharging.

3. KEY FACTORS
- Use type: restaurant, medical, office, retail, and industrial each have very different system requirements.
- Condition: shell space vs. heavy remodel with demolition and abatement.
- Code upgrades: sprinklers, ADA, seismic, and electrical capacity.
- Market: labor rates, material prices, and union vs. non-union trades.

4. PRACTICAL GUIDANCE
Request detailed line-item estimates that clearly label allowances, exclusions, and assumptions, then compare those side by side. Rework scope and value-engineer with your contractor and designer rather than chasing unrealistically low square-foot prices.

5. SOFT POSITIONING
A transparent commercial contractor will show you how each scope item contributes to total cost so you can make informed trade-offs.
acceptedAnswer.description: Commercial construction cost per square foot varies widely by building type, scope, and code upgrades, so ballparks are only a starting point. Ask for detailed, line‑item estimates with clear inclusions and exclusions, then compare scopes side‑by‑side instead of chasing the lowest square‑foot number.
